principle: Consumer adoption is external to the consumer scaffold. The governance repository owns selection and immutable lock state; an execution receipt binds that lock to an exact consumer source SHA.

requirements: asset id and requested version are explicit
asset is already QUALIFIED in governance main
consumer scaffold and Yunka version are not implicit dependencies of adoption

lock.rule: Every execution uses exact immutable identities from the active lock; path names alone are not authority.

verification.sourceBinding: Every receipt records the exact consumer commit that was checked.
required: active lock resolves without identity drift
static recurrence guard executes on declared consumer paths
authoritative behavior regression executes when the prevention asset declares one
consumer tracked source and dependency locks remain unchanged

upgrade.policyDelta: difference between old and candidate governance asset/tool identities on the same consumer source
upgrade.codeDelta: difference between base and head consumer source under the same governance lock
rules: a no-op candidate is NO_CHANGE, never reported as an upgrade
a candidate with nonexistent/unqualified version or mismatched immutable blob is REJECTED
tool version changes require their own admitted tool identity
a version-changing upgrade is not claimed until a distinct qualified asset version exists
activation is an explicit lock replacement after candidate verification

rollback.rule: Rollback can select only a previously qualified immutable lock identity.
rollback.behavior: A rejected candidate leaves the active lock unchanged; explicit rollback resolves the prior lock before activation.
